terms.definition: A vertical column of the periodic table whose elements share the same number of valence electrons.
terms.function: Groups elements that behave alike so their properties can be predicted from their column position.
terms.whereItIs: The glowing vertical column of tiles in the model.
terms.whyItMatters: The group number is one of the quickest predictions of an element's behavior in all of chemistry.

terms.definition: The electrons in the outermost shell of an atom — the ones that control bonding.
terms.function: Decide how many bonds an atom forms and how reactive it is; shared down each group.
terms.whereItIs: The small shells shown beside each tile in the valence-highlight layer.
terms.whyItMatters: Shared valence electrons are the reason elements in a column behave alike.

terms.definition: The elements of Group 1 — soft, shiny metals with one valence electron, known for high reactivity.
terms.function: React readily because each atom wants to shed its single outer electron.
terms.whereItIs: The first column of the periodic table.
terms.whyItMatters: They are the textbook example of a group whose members all behave alike.

terms.definition: The elements of Group 18 — gases with full outer shells that almost never react.
terms.function: Remain unreactive because their full shells leave no need to gain or lose electrons.
terms.whereItIs: The last column of the periodic table.
terms.whyItMatters: They show the other extreme of group behavior — the calm mirror of the reactive alkali metals.
